audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for John's question, Jesus' signs, wilderness prophet language, Elijah motif, generation critique, woes to cities, hidden/revealed wisdom, Father/Son knowing, and rest/yoke invitation.

verses.restored: When Jesus finished instructing his twelve disciples, he departed from there to teach and proclaim in their cities.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Jesus had made an end of commanding his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and to preach in their cities.

verses.restored: John, hearing in prison the works of the Messiah, sent through his disciples

familiar.text: Now when John had heard in the prison the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples,

verses.restored: and said to him, Are you the coming one, or should we look for another?

familiar.text: And said unto him, Art thou he that should come, or do we look for another?

verses.restored: Jesus answered them, Go report to John what you hear and see:

familiar.text: Jesus answered and said unto them, Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see:

verses.restored: the blind receive sight, the lame walk, those with skin disease are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor are given good news.

familiar.text: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.

verses.restored: Blessed/flourishing is the one who is not caused to stumble by me.

familiar.text: And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.

verses.restored: As they were going away, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: What did you go out into the wilderness to behold? A reed shaken by wind?

familiar.text: And as they departed, Jesus began to say unto the multitudes concerning John, What went ye out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken with the wind?

verses.restored: But what did you go out to see? A person clothed in soft garments? Look, those wearing soft garments are in kings' houses.

familiar.text: But what went ye out for to see? A man clothed in soft raiment? behold, they that wear soft clothing are in kings’ houses.

verses.restored: But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.

familiar.text: But what went ye out for to see? A prophet? yea, I say unto you, and more than a prophet.

verses.restored: This is the one about whom it has been written: Look, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you.

familiar.text: For this is he, of whom it is written, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

verses.restored: Amen, I say to you: among those born of women, none has arisen greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the reign of the heavens is greater than he.

familiar.text: Verily I say unto you, Among them that are born of women there hath not risen a greater than John the Baptist: notwithstanding he that is least in the kingdom of heaven is greater than he.

verses.restored: From the days of John the Baptist until now, the reign of the heavens is forcefully pressing forward, and forceful ones seize/press into it.

familiar.text: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.

verses.restored: For all the Prophets and the Law prophesied until John.

familiar.text: For all the prophets and the law prophesied until John.

verses.restored: And if you are willing to receive it, he is Elijah who is to come.

familiar.text: And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.

verses.restored: The one having ears, let him hear.

familiar.text: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

verses.restored: To what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, calling to others,

familiar.text: But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the markets, and calling unto their fellows,

verses.restored: We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we lamented, and you did not mourn.

familiar.text: And saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned unto you, and ye have not lamented.

verses.restored: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He has an unclean spirit.

familiar.text: For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a devil.

verses.restored: The Son of Humanity came eating and drinking, and they say, Look, a glutton and wine-drinker, friend of tax collectors and sinners. Yet wisdom is justified by her works.

familiar.text: The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.

verses.restored: Then he began to reproach the cities in which most of his powers had happened, because they did not turn/realign.

familiar.text: Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not:

verses.restored: Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the powers that happened in you had happened in Tyre and Sidon, long ago they would have turned in sackcloth and ashes.

familiar.text: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.

verses.restored: But I say to you: it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon in the day of judgment than for you.

familiar.text: But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.

verses.restored: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted to heaven? You will go down to Hades. For if the powers that happened in you had happened in Sodom, it would have remained until today.

familiar.text: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.

verses.restored: But I say to you: it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for you.

familiar.text: But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.

verses.restored: At that time Jesus answered and said, I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you hid these things from wise and understanding ones and revealed them to infants.

familiar.text: At that time Jesus answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.

verses.restored: Yes, Father, because this became good pleasure before you.

familiar.text: Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in thy sight.

verses.restored: All things have been handed over to me by my Father; no one fully knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone fully know the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wills to reveal him.

familiar.text: All things are delivered unto me of my Father: and no man knoweth the Son, but the Father; neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.

verses.restored: Come to me, all who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest.

familiar.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.

verses.restored: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls/lives.

familiar.text: Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.

verses.restored: For my yoke is kind/useful, and my burden is light.

familiar.text: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
